Title: Tests run at the fastest free place and every run records its outcome

## For the human
- **What:** в orch-it появляется запуск тестов: каждый прогон идёт в одно из мест для тестов (своя машина, другая машина из настроек, GitHub), место выбирает одно правило по измеренному времени, а сам прогон пишется в хранилище событий вместе с местом, временем и итогом: прошёл, упал или без результата.
- **Goal:** тесты любого репо на любой машине идут туда, где закончатся раньше, оборванный прогон никогда не считается падением, а владелец и мозг видят по хранилищу, где тесты шли, сколько ждали и где узкое место, без ручных замеров.
- **Plan:** один сильный агент с помощниками, как в части 1: запуск тестов в чистом окружении с чтением стандартного отчёта о тестах, правило выбора места, другая машина через SSH, загрузка прогонов GitHub в хранилище, ночной полный прогон; каждая часть вливается через пулл-реквест, зелёный на Linux и Windows.
- **Result:** 6 из 6 исходов прогона распознаны верно (зелёный, красный, оборван по времени, 0 тестов, не найдены заказанные тесты, нет отчёта), и ни один оборванный прогон не записан как падение; правило места даёт одинаковый выбор на Linux и Windows на 12+ случаях с посчитанным вручную ответом; прогон на другой машине через SSH не трогает рабочую папку вызвавшего; повторная загрузка прогонов GitHub добавляет 0 событий; случай вне названных: отчёты двух инструментов тестов не на Python читаются так же, как отчёт pytest; в закрывающем комментарии — время прогона и ожидание очереди GitHub по каждому месту и ОС из хранилища и расход самой части.
- **Undo:** two-way door (новый код в новом репо, старый слой не трогается); touches orch-it, его проверки на Linux и Windows и машины, названные в настройках как места для тестов.

## For the agent

Weight: 8

Step: part 2 of the rebuild order (#387 resolution, comment 6398337229): "test runs and the test-place rule: outcome passed / failed / no result, run time per place from the store". Waits on part 1 (#393, the event store: its writer API, closed-set file and `docs/events.md`), which is why it is blocked by #393. Driver: one strong agent with helpers, the same form as #393: an Opus 5.5 high background session in the orch-it checkout, own worktree; the outcome rules (decision 2) and the place rule (decision 5) are the strong agent's own units, the importer, CLI and workflow may go to Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 helpers. The old repo is read only as a source of cases, never copied (#387).

### Decided by the brain (with reasons)

1. **A test run is one call of the repo's test command at one place, on one commit, read from its JUnit XML report.** The command is a setting (`test_command`, default pytest writing `--junitxml`), the report path a setting. Reason: JUnit XML is written by pytest, jest-junit, go-junit-report, gotestsum, Maven Surefire and most other runners, so a stranger's repo in any language is read the same way; parsing pytest's text output would bind the layer to one tool.
2. **Outcome rules** (the strong agent's unit), every run writes a `test_run` pair and one `test.result` per test case:

   | outcome | when | reason code |
   |---|---|---|
   | `passed` | complete report, collected > 0, every requested id collected, 0 failed or errored | - |
   | `failed` | complete report with at least one failed or errored case (red at any required place is red; a local green is evidence only, TEST-7) | `red` |
   | `no_result` | the run hit its bound (setting `test_run_bound_minutes`, default 15) and its process tree was killed | `cut` (`suspended` when the machine slept across the bound) |
   | `no_result` | collected 0 | `none_collected` |
   | `no_result` | an id from the ids file was not collected | `ids_not_collected` |
   | `no_result` | no report, or a report that is half-written or does not parse | `summary_missing` |
   | `no_result` | a required OS job of a GitHub run is absent | `job_missing` |
   | `refused` | the place could not take the run | `busy`, `os_missing`, `place_off`, `out_of_minutes` |
   | `lost` | the place vanished mid-run | `place_vanished` |
   | `stopped` | a newer push cancelled the run; only the newer head's result counts (TEST-12) | `superseded` |

   The new reason codes are added to part 1's closed-set file and to `docs/events.md` in the same change, so part 1's agreement test holds.
3. **Clean environment** (TEST-15, #383): the test process gets only the OS's base variables (one fixed list per OS in the package: the path, home, temp and system-root names) plus the setting `test_env`; nothing else of the caller's environment. `settings_hash` in `test_run` covers the command, the bound and `test_env`.
4. **Test places** (#378 area 1): `own` (always); `machine:<id>`, one per entry of the per-machine settings (`host` reached by plain `ssh`, `os`, `checkout` folder, `capacity`); `github` when the setting `github_tests` is on. A machine place checks out the exact commit in its own folder (fetched from the origin) and never touches the caller's work tree. Reason for SSH: OpenSSH ships with Windows 10 and later, Linux and macOS, so a stranger installs nothing on the far machine but git, Python and the repo's test dependencies.
5. **The place rule** (the strong agent's unit). Inputs: the OS the run needs (`linux`, `windows`, `macos` or `any`), the places, live runs per place counted from the store (`test_run` started with no `ended`, younger than the bound plus a grace), measured durations from the store. In order: drop a place without that OS (`os_missing`), switched off (`place_off`), at capacity (`busy`, TEST-9); for each place left, expected finish = start overhead (median of its measured starts) + run time (median of its last 10 ended `passed` / `failed` runs of the same repo and selection); a place with no measured run takes the own place's median, and with nothing measured anywhere the run goes to `own`; ties go own, then machines in settings order, then github; no place left writes a `wait` with reason `test_place`. The decision rides in the `test_run` detail: `places_offered` (each with expected finish in minutes or its drop reason), `chosen`, `reason`. Load is the count of live runs read from the store, never the OS's CPU load: it reads the same on every OS and replays from the store (#378: "one measured rule that reads load the same way on Windows, Linux and macOS").
6. **Required checks stay the gate and run the full suite on `linux` and `windows` on every pull request** (TEST-3, TEST-4: selection never decides a required check). No test selection and no split into parts in this part. Reason: orch-it's suite runs in minutes; a split adds jobs per pull request, and GitHub caps concurrent jobs per account, so it adds queue rather than removing it; a selection map is a second source of truth to keep correct. The owner's worry (no bottleneck on GitHub's machines, #389 resolution "Open") is answered by measurement: the `test-places` query (decision 9) shows the median run and the median GitHub queue wait per place and OS, and when either passes the bound a ticket is opened from those numbers. #378's "Windows the thin system module per change" is held to the same measurement: until the Windows full run nears its bound there is nothing to thin.
7. **GitHub runs reach the store through an importer on the local side**: `events import-github` reads the repo's workflow runs and jobs through `gh`, writes per job a `test_run` pair (place `github`, `os` from the job, commit = head sha, branch, PR, `billed_minutes` from the run's timing), the time from queued to started as a `wait` with reason `github_queue`, and the per-test `test.result` rows from the JUnit artifact each job uploads. GitHub conclusions map to decision 2's outcomes (success to passed; failure to failed when the report holds a failure, else `summary_missing`; cancelled to stopped `superseded` when a newer run of the same branch exists; timed out to `cut`). Event ids are a hash of (run id, job id, attempt, kind), so a re-import writes nothing new (as part 1's decision 5).
8. **Workflow**: the job names `linux` and `windows` stay (branch protection requires them by name); each job uploads its JUnit report; a nightly `schedule` run (and `workflow_dispatch`) runs the full suite with the tests marked `slow` and `live` (TEST-14); pull request and push runs leave those marks out.
9. **CLI**: `python -m orch_it tests run [--os ...] [--ids-file ...] [--place ...]` (a forced place is for a human; the default is the rule), `events import-github`, and the named query `test-places`: per place and OS, runs, outcomes, median run minutes, median GitHub queue minutes.
10. **Record**: `GLOSSARY.md` gains only this part's words (test run, test place, place rule, clean environment, bound); `docs/adr/0002` holds decisions 1, 5 and 6 (the load measure and the full-suite gate are surprising and costly to undo).

### Acceptance

| row | check | pass |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | outcomes, own place, in the `linux` and the `windows` job | fixture suites: green gives passed; one red gives failed with that id in `test.result`; a test sleeping past a 1-minute bound gives no_result `cut` with 0 processes of the run left; 0 collected gives `none_collected`; an ids file naming a missing id gives `ids_not_collected`; a deleted or truncated report gives `summary_missing`: 6 of 6, and no no_result case writes failed |
| 2 | outside case: runners other than pytest | real JUnit reports produced by jest-junit and go-junit-report (committed fixtures with their tool versions) give the same outcomes and per-test rows as pytest's report of the same results |
| 3 | clean environment, both jobs | a variable set in the caller's environment and not in `test_env` is absent in the test process; one from `test_env` is present; `settings_hash` changes when `test_env` changes |
| 4 | the place rule, both jobs | a table of at least 12 cases with hand-computed picks covers each drop reason, the tie order, a place with no measurement, nothing measured anywhere, and no place left (a `wait` with `test_place`); the same table passes on Linux and Windows; every decision lists every offered place with its expected finish or drop reason |
| 5 | a machine place over SSH, `linux` job | an sshd on localhost configured as `machine:local-ssh`: a run at a given commit checks it out in that machine's folder, the caller's `git status` is identical before and after, the result lands in the caller's store with place `machine:local-ssh` and the outcome own gives; the sshd killed mid-run gives lost `place_vanished`, the rule's next place reruns it, and no failed is written |
| 6 | GitHub importer on orch-it's real runs | every job of this part's pull requests has a `test_run` pair with its mapped outcome and its `github_queue` wait; a second import adds 0 events; a run cancelled by a newer push gives stopped `superseded`; a fixture run holding only one of the two required jobs gives no_result `job_missing`; per-test rows equal each job's collected count |
| 7 | workflow | job names `linux` and `windows` unchanged and this part's pull requests merge under the same protection; one nightly run (scheduled or dispatched) collects the `slow` and `live` tests, a pull request run collects 0 of them |
| 8 | closed sets | the new reason codes are in the closed-set file and `docs/events.md`; the agreement test passes, and a code planted in only one of them fails it |
| 9 | the owner-visible result | `test-places` over orch-it's real runs and `session-cost` over this part's own sessions posted in the closing comment: per place and OS runs, outcomes, median run and GitHub queue minutes; $, % week and tokens per session and model; minutes as minutes |
| 10 | how it lands | every unit a pull request to orch-it merged green on `linux` and `windows`; each diff reviewed on the Standards, Spec and edge-input axes (#381) with findings and fixes counted; report lines `tdd`, `codebase-design`, `domain-modeling` per the skill table |

Outside case: test reports from runners other than pytest (jest-junit, go-junit-report; row 2): every case named above runs pytest, and a reader bound to pytest's output or exit codes reads a stranger's JavaScript or Go repo as `summary_missing` or as green.
Same object: orch-it's `.github/workflows/tests.yml` is read by branch protection (#392), which requires the checks `linux` and `windows` by name: a renamed job would block every pull request, so decision 8 keeps both names (row 7). Part 1's store, closed-set file and `docs/events.md` (#393) are owned by part 1: this part writes through part 1's writer API and adds reason codes through the same file and agreement test (row 8); part 1's transcript importer writes other kinds into the same store with distinct ids, so both run without effect on each other. The GitHub Actions API is only read here. Part 1's session writes in orch-it until #393 closes; this part starts after that, so orch-it never has two writers at once.
Not in this ticket: who merges and what happens on red with GitHub off, the red-on-main ticket, the ticket that follows its pull request (part 5); ORCH's acceptance step and the `after merge` mark (parts 4 and 5); sharing GitHub's machines between several repos by priority (part 8, needs a second installed repo); test copies for a private repo (#378: decided when the other repos are rebuilt); test selection and splitting into parts (decision 6); the monitor's views (part 7).
